title: Melbourne Trivia Night

questions.q: Melbourne is the capital of which Australian state?
Which river flows through the centre of Melbourne?
Which sporting ground, known to locals as "the G", hosts the AFL Grand Final?
The Melbourne Cup is run on the first Tuesday of which month?
In which year did Melbourne host the Summer Olympic Games?
Melburnians arrange to meet "under the clocks" at which railway station?
Which champion racehorse of the early 1930s is on display at Melbourne Museum?
Which bushranger was hanged at the Old Melbourne Gaol in 1880?
Which long-running soap, filmed in Melbourne's suburbs, was set on Ramsay Street?
Which building in Carlton Gardens hosted the opening of Australia's first federal parliament in 1901?

notes: Melbourne is the capital of Victoria; see Victorian Government / Wikipedia 'Melbourne'.
The Yarra River runs through the Melbourne CBD; see Wikipedia 'Yarra River' / Melbourne Water.
MCG, nicknamed 'the G', traditional home of the AFL Grand Final; see mcg.org.au / Wikipedia 'Melbourne Cricket Ground'.
Melbourne Cup run on the first Tuesday in November at Flemington; see Victoria Racing Club / Wikipedia 'Melbourne Cup'.
1956 Summer Olympics held in Melbourne (Nov to Dec 1956); see olympics.com / Wikipedia '1956 Summer Olympics'.
'Meet me under the clocks' refers to the clocks over the main entrance of Flinders Street Station; see Wikipedia 'Flinders Street railway station'.
Phar Lap (raced 1928 to 1932); his mounted hide is displayed at Melbourne Museum; see Museums Victoria / Wikipedia 'Phar Lap'.
Ned Kelly hanged at Old Melbourne Gaol on 11 November 1880; see National Trust Old Melbourne Gaol / Wikipedia 'Ned Kelly'.
Neighbours (1985-2025); ended December 2025, hence past tense.
First Parliament of Australia opened at the Royal Exhibition Building on 9 May 1901; see Museums Victoria / UNESCO World Heritage listing.
